title: Lanthanide-containing clusters for catalytic water splitting and CO2 conversion
claim: Homogeneous LnCC HER catalysts are limited by a narrow photoresponse and difficult recovery, whereas anchoring atomically precise Ln–transition-metal clusters on a semiconductor can improve charge separation, supply HER sites, and ease recycling.
explanation: The review contrasts molecular LnCCs with Ln52Ni56−xCdx clusters bound to CdS by partial replacement of cluster Ni by Cd from the support. The cluster both separates charge and acts as the HER site, giving 25353 μmol g−1 h−1 for the Eu composite under visible light.
scope: Supported Ln52Ni56−xCdx/CdS composites versus homogeneous LnCC photocatalysts.
conditions: Visible light, λ > 420 nm, Na2S/Na2SO3 in water.
caveats: The high rate is specific to the Eu composite; Pr, Nd, and Gd analogues do not open the same second electron-transfer path.
